inputs.text:
Five months after a hollow ceasefire announcement, we are seeing the uninterrupted devastation of the Palestinian people—a profound moral failure born from systemic violence, institutional complicity, and the relentless oppression of a marginalized and vulnerable population. Airstrikes and military aggression continue to slaughter civilians while the humanitarian crisis is intentionally left to fester. This is nothing less than the structural erasure of a community, designed to strip working people and families of their history, dignity, and basic human rights. 

As 56-year-old Ahmed Baroud, a father of five currently displaced in Deir al-Balah, powerfully pointed out: “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen.” 

This state brutality is reducing human existence to a nightmare entirely disconnected from any prewar reality. The international institutions and power structures that refuse to enforce true justice and dismantle these systems of oppression must be held fully accountable for their complicit inaction in the face of such profound injustice.
